BEHAVIORAL RISK FACTOR

Alcohol Consumption and Cardiovascular Disease

Alcohol is another major behavioral exposure linked to cardiovascular disease. It is associated with higher blood pressure, arrhythmia, and increased risk of heart disease and stroke.

Alcohol-attributable cardiovascular burden

worldwide CVD deaths attributable to alcohol in 2019

diseases and injuries associated with harmful alcohol use

4.2 million

CVD deaths in the WHO European Region in 2019

Alcohol consumption → increased blood pressure → cardiovascular damage → higher risk of heart disease or stroke

Alcohol use contributes to hypertension, arrhythmia, and coronary disease. It is an important behavioral predictor to compare across countries and over time.
